clue.text: Credit unavailable for carpet

parts.note: to tick an item is to give it credit or mark it as correct
a dish that is off is no longer available

explanation.surface: A shop refuses credit on a carpet purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is a verb here, as in being called on the carpet by the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to scold or reprimand someone for a fault.

clue.text: Monkey with pub, not new, south of river

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below, south of, the first

parts.note: the Tamar is the river between Devon and Cornwall in England

indicators.note: not removes the named letter from the word before it

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A monkey heads to a pub below a river crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' drops one N from INN to leave IN. 'South of' places it under TAMAR in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tamarin is a small South American monkey.

clue.text: Chirpy chap turns up with normal line

parts.note: to cock a hat brim or an ear is to turn it up
par is the normal or average standard
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A cheerful fellow tilts his hat up while standing in an orderly queue.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is an informal name for a cheeky, perky little man, likened to a male bird.

clue.text: Most of fortune built up within a month? Very mysterious

indicators.note: within says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October

indicators.note: built up in a down entry means the letters are placed upwards, so reversed
most of asks for the word less its last letter

parts.note: luck means fortune

explanation.surface: Someone builds most of their wealth within a single month, which seems inexplicable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the last letter of the fortune word; 'built up' reads what is left upwards, as this is a down entry; 'within' puts it inside the month abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Occult means hidden, supernatural, beyond ordinary understanding.

clue.text: Rich woman's punctual, maybe meeting old man at Lord's

parts.note: rich food is fat
her is the possessive for a woman
being punctual is being on time

explanation.surface: A wealthy woman arrives promptly to meet an elderly gentleman at the cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground; its weathervane shows the old bearded figure removing the bails.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded figure with a scythe personifies time, and his likeness forms the weathervane at the cricket ground.

clue.text: Couplet appears sadistic, horribly partial

indicators.note: partial says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rhyming pair of lines seems cruel and terribly biased.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Couplet appears' as the definition, but 'appears' is a link word joining definition to wordplay and cannot stand in for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A distich is a pair of verse lines, a technical term for a two-line unit of poetry.

clue.text: Blue feathers

definitions.meaning: feeling blue is feeling sad or low
the soft fine plumage of birds

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is depressed in mood; the other is the fluffy plumage of young birds.

clue.text: A wise man must take medication as a result of accident

indicators.note: must take says the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
a pill is a dose of medication

explanation.surface: A wise man is forced to swallow pills after a mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: A spill of liquid or goods is what follows when something is knocked over by mistake.

clue.text: Fluid form of writing

parts.note: sounds like flowing handwriting, but means writing in its liquid state, the stuff in a pen

explanation.definitionFit: The coloured liquid used in pens is writing in liquid form.

clue.text: Car difficult to beat

parts.note: hard means difficult
to top something is to beat or surpass it

explanation.surface: A vehicle that is hard to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardtop is a car with a rigid roof, often a removable one.

clue.text: Protection from cats and dogs

parts.note: it is raining cats and dogs means pouring rain, so the protection is a raincoat, not a fence against pets

explanation.definitionFit: A mackintosh is a waterproof coat that keeps off heavy rain.

clue.text: Component of old radio, not quite the best

indicators.note: not quite asks for the phrase with its final letter left off

parts.note: the cat's whiskers is a dated idiom for something excellent

explanation.surface: A piece of a vintage wireless set falls just short of excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the final S of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Early crystal radio sets used a fine wire contact, called by this name, touching the crystal detector.

clue.text: Not put off, tackled crossword again?

definitions.meaning: determined, firm in purpose and undeterred
read as ..., worked out the puzzle a second time

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is firmly determined; the other splits as re-solved, solved a second time.

clue.text: Fail to appear during court recess

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the span of the other

parts.note: to lose a contest is to fail in it

explanation.surface: Someone fails to turn up while the court has adjourned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' looks like part of the court picture, a break in proceedings, but it is the definition: an alcove or cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard set into a wall is a small enclosed recess.

clue.text: American chief in session, talking nonsense

parts.note: a sitting is a session of a court or parliament
bull is slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: A US leader in a meeting is speaking rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting Bull was a Lakota Sioux leader who fought at Little Bighorn.

clue.text: An indication of the flow of time

definitions.text: An indication of the flow of time

parts.words: An indication of the flow of time
parts.note: the passing of time is metaphorical, but here a real flow of liquid shows the hours

explanation.definitionFit: An ancient timekeeper that measures hours by the steady dripping of liquid.

clue.text: Excellent American cattle

definitions.meaning: in US slang something ... is great or excellent
an old word for oxen or bovine livestock

explanation.definitionFit: The word is American slang for great, and an archaic collective term for oxen.

clue.text: On the level? Yes and no

definitions.text: On the level? Yes and no

parts.words: On the level? Yes and no
parts.note: on the level means honest, which fits; but taken literally, upright is not level at all

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means honestly or truthfully, while literally it describes something vertical rather than flat.

clue.text: Edward's uncle got over slight depression with zeal

indicators.note: got over says the first piece lies over, around, the second

parts.note: Edward Lear wrote a poem about his Uncle Arly
a dent is a slight hollow

explanation.surface: A relative recovers from mild gloom with fresh enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got over' looks like recovering from something, and 'slight depression' suggests a low mood; really one piece wraps over the other, and the depression is a small hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardently means passionately, with great enthusiasm.

clue.text: Vacillating, or remind HM of certain spectacles?

indicators.note: vacillating means wavering to and fro, so these letters are shifted about

explanation.surface: An indecisive person is told to remind the monarch about some glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacillating' rearranges OR REMIND HM; HM is His or Her Majesty.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasses with frames made of horn or an imitation of it are described this way.

clue.text: Ring with information to support a certain element

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: a halo is a ring of light
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A ring and some data back up a particular chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Chlorine, fluorine and iodine belong to this group of the periodic table.

clue.text: Left friend in Paris, returning to another capital

indicators.note: returning tells us to read the French word backwards

parts.note: ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a French friend behind and travels back to a different city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns AMI into IMA. Paris is itself a capital, which is why the answer is 'another'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru.

clue.text: Shortly to receive, military award, etc

indicators.note: to receive says the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: anon is an old word meaning shortly or soon
the DSO is the Distinguished Service Order, a British military decoration

explanation.surface: Someone is due shortly to collect a medal, and so forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Etc is the abbreviation for et cetera, meaning the list continues likewise.

clue.text: Pout entering ship, appearing sweet

indicators.note: entering says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a moue is a pout
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A sulking passenger boards a ship and is offered dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly SS goes into MOUE, the reverse of what the surface suggests; the clue reads the pout as entering into a combination with the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousse is a light whipped dessert.

clue.text: 1'I'll have a brief look for new suit

definitions.text: I'll have a brief look for new suit

parts.words: I'll have a brief look for new suit
parts.note: sounds like a shopper glancing for clothes, but a brief is a legal case and a suit is a lawsuit

explanation.definitionFit: A barrister or solicitor takes on briefs and seeks out fresh lawsuits.

clue.text: Creating a disaster?

parts.note: the divine work of Creation, and in insurance terms a natural catastrophe nobody can be blamed for

explanation.definitionFit: Insurers use the phrase for floods, storms and other natural catastrophes beyond human control.

clue.text: Somewhat undervalued fuel

indicators.note: somewhat says only part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Fuel that is a little underpriced.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV is British diesel fuel for road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Derv is the British name for diesel oil used in road vehicles.

clue.text: Deteriorate, having acquired mostly different setters?

parts.note: got means acquired or obtained

indicators.note: mostly asks for the word with its last letter removed

parts.note: other means different
setters are a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: Things slide downhill after acquiring a fresh team of crossword compilers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setters' suggests crossword compilers, but they are dogs. 'Mostly' trims OTHER to OTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to decline badly or fall into ruin.

clue.text: Salt lake finally drained desert arises

indicators.note: arises in a down entry means the word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to rat on someone is to desert them; the run of letters across the two words is a coincidence, not the setter's hiding place

explanation.surface: A salt lake dries up at last and desert rises in its place.
explanation.walkthrough: A salt is an old sailor. 'Arises' turns RAT upwards. 'Lake finally drained' gives the answer again: TARN (a mountain lake) losing its final N.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are old nicknames for a seaman.

clue.text: "Unusual, futuristic and otherworldly' starts to describe it

definitions.text: "Unusual, futuristic and otherworldly' starts to describe it

indicators.note: starts asks for the opening letter of each of the quoted words

explanation.surface: A description of a flying saucer built from three apt adjectives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts' takes the first letters of the three quoted adjectives, and the whole clue also describes the thing.
explanation.definitionFit: An unidentified flying object is often imagined as an alien spacecraft, strange and from another world.

clue.text: Dash back to gaze at very good dancer

indicators.note: back says that word is written backwards

parts.note: to dash is to run
to eye something is to gaze at it
V for very good is a common marking abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone hurries back to admire an outstanding performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Nureyev was a celebrated Soviet-born ballet star.

clue.text: Half remain with king, and none back government

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: half asks for the first three of the six letters of the word that follows
back says that word is written backwards

parts.note: nil means none or nothing

explanation.surface: Half stay loyal to the king and none support the ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moscow citadel stands by metonymy for the Russian administration.
